messages.content: Identify the number of the mitochondria in a cell.

message.content:
The exact number of mitochondria varies widely between cell types and even within the same cell type under different conditions. In general:

| Cell type | Typical range of mitochondria per cell |
|-----------|----------------------------------------|
| **Red blood cells** (which lack mitochondria) | 0 |
| **Neurons** | ~10–100 000 (highly active neurons can have tens of thousands) |
| **Muscle cells (skeletal, cardiac)** | ~10 000–50 000 (cardiac myocytes often have >30 000) |
| **Epithelial cells** | ~1 000–10 000 |
| **Stem cells** | ~500–5 000 |
| **Cancer cells** | Variable; often increased due to high metabolic demand |

These numbers are approximate averages. A single cell can contain anywhere from a few dozen to several hundred thousand mitochondria, depending on its energy requirements, differentiation state, and environmental conditions.
